youtube.title: Iran's Mountains: A Wall With Two Gaps
youtube.description:
America invaded both of Iran's neighbours, Afghanistan and Iraq, within two years, but never Iran. Why is Iran so hard to invade, and how much of the answer is simply the map? Two mountain ranges, the Zagros and the Elburz, wrap around a high plateau where most of Iran's 90 million people live, and that wall has two gaps: the flat oil plain of Khuzestan in the southwest and the open ground of the northeast.

This episode measures the wall and its gaps, then follows the lines they drew, from Alexander at the Persian Gates in 330 BC to the 1639 Treaty of Zuhab and the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War. Then it sets out what Washington and Tehran each say they want today, the 1941 precedent that cuts the other way, and three paths that could change the map.

{CHAPTERS}
